algorithms.name: Exp3.G
requires_knowledge_of: weakly dominating set D and its size (weakly observable case)

source.label: th:mainupper
source.quote: if $G$ is strongly observable, then for $U=V$, $\gamma = \min\bigl\{ \bigl(\tfrac{1}{\alpha T}\bigr)^{1/2} , \tfrac{1}{2} \bigr\}$ and $\eta =  2\gamma ,$ the expected regret against any loss sequence is $\O( \alpha^{1/2} T^{1/2} \ln(KT) )$;

results.notes: Losses fixed against a specific loss sequence (oblivious); regret E[sum loss] - min_i sum loss equals expected regret for oblivious adversary.

source.label: th:mainupper
source.quote: if $G$ is weakly observable and $T \ge K^3 \ln(K) / \del^2$, then for $U=D$, $\gamma = \min\!\big\{ \big(\tfrac{\delta\ln K}{T}\big)^{1/3}, \tfrac{1}{2} \big\}$ and $\eta = \tfrac{\gamma^{2}}{\delta} ,$ the~expected regret against any loss sequence is $\O\bigl( (\delta\ln K)^{1/3}T^{2/3} \bigr) .$

results.notes: Computing a minimum weakly dominating set may be hard in general; per-round update is polynomial given D.

conditions: G is the loopless clique (all edges except self-loops)

source.label: th:blind
source.quote: For any sequence of loss functions $\ell_{1},\ldots,\ell_{T}$, where $\ell_t:V \mapsto [0, 1]$, the regret of \cref{alg:alg}, with the loopless clique feedback graph and with parameters $\eta = \sqrt{(\ln K)/(2T)}$ and $\gamma=2\eta$, is upper-bounded by $5\sqrt{T\ln K}$.

results.notes: Loopless clique is strongly observable with alpha=1; learner does not need alpha here.

source.label: th:notobser
source.quote: If $G=(V,E)$ is not observable and $\abs{V} \ge 2$, then for any player algorithm there exists a sequence of loss functions $\ell_{1},\ell_2,\ldots : V \mapsto [0,1]$ such that the player's expected regret is at least~$\tfrac{1}{4} T$.

results.notes: The proof ends with 'at least 1/8 T, as claimed', inconsistent with statement's 1/4 T; recorded the statement. Also yields Theorem 1(iii) Theta(T).

source.label: th:lower-weak
source.quote: If $G=(V,E)$ is weakly observable with $K = \abs{V} \ge 2$ and weak domination number $\del = \del(G)$, then for any randomized player algorithm and for any time horizon $T$ there exists a sequence of loss functions $\ell_{1},\ldots,\ell_{T} : V \mapsto [0,1]$ such that the player's expected regret is at least $\tfrac{1}{150} \bigl(\del/\ln^2\!{K}\bigr)^{1/3} T^{2/3} .$

results.notes: Proof uses stochastic Bernoulli losses then derandomizes; holds also with binary losses.

source.label: th:weakobserv
source.quote: If $G=(V,E)$ is weakly observable and $\abs{V} \ge 2$, then for any player algorithm and for any time horizon $T$ there exists a sequence of loss functions $\ell_{1},\ldots,\ell_{T} : V \mapsto [0,1]$ such that the player's expected regret is at least $\tfrac{1}{8} T^{2/3}$.

conditions: graphs G_t weakly observable with weak domination number and independence number equal to 1 for all t
graphs revealed after the action (uninformed model)

source.label: th:weak-sep
source.quote: For any randomized player strategy in the uninformed feedback model, there exists a sequence of weakly observable graphs $G_{1},\ldots,G_{T}$ over a set $V$ of $K \ge 4$ actions with $\del(G_t)=\alpha(G_t)=1$ for all $t$, and a sequence of loss functions $\ell_{1},\ldots,\ell_{T} : V \mapsto [0,1]$, such that the player's expected regret is at least $\tfrac{1}{16} K^{1/3} T^{2/3}$.

results.notes: Graph sequence is constructed randomly and independently of the learner (oblivious).

conditions: G strongly observable, fixed and known

source.label: th:main
source.quote: Then the minimax regret of the $T$-round online learning problem induced by $G$, where $T \ge |V|^3$, is (i) $R(G,T) = \wt{\Theta}(\alpha^{1/2} \, T^{1/2})$ if $G$ is strongly observable; (ii) $R(G,T) = \wt{\Theta}(\delta^{1/3} \, T^{2/3})$ if $G$ is weakly observable; (iii) $R(G,T) = \Theta(T)$ if $G$ is not observable.

results.notes: Lower-bound half of Theorem 1(i), derived from Alon et al. 2014 Theorem 5 extended to graphs missing self-loops (footnote). Upper halves and (ii),(iii) covered by Theorems 2, 6, 7.
